cause: Unknown; the leading hypothesis is intermittent digitizer or DAQ readout loss downstream of otherwise active LVDS signals.
action: First map missing channels by subrun to digitizer boards and inspect raw event/channel presence, digitizer status, synchronization, DAQ restart/error, CPU, and queue logs. Compare digitizer event rates with trigger-board rates. If the missing channels form a board-aligned group and a lockup or synchronization failure is confirmed, stop the run and restart/resynchronize the affected digitizer/DAQ process; reboot the associated DAQ PC only if standard restart does not clear it. Do not replace PMT/HV or LVDS hardware without corresponding HV or pin-level evidence.

The count transition near subrun 40 occurs without a comparable rate transition and may reflect exposure length rather than detector failure. INFERRED: broad channel loss with healthy LVDS activity is more consistent with downstream digitizer/readout dropout than a trigger-board, LVDS-pin, or isolated PMT-base fault. Run 1620 is a partial digitizer-lockup analogy; runs 1500 and 1604 provide weaker DAQ-restart analogies.
